_note: A dependant with disability: s.127(1): a resident individual "shall be allowed a deduction up to ₹ 75000 … if during that year he has (a) incurred expenditure for the medical treatment (including nursing), training and rehabilitation of a dependant, being a person with disability; or (b) paid or deposited any amount under a scheme … for the maintenance of a dependant" (pp.162–163); "dependant" — the spouse, children, parents, brothers and sisters "dependant wholly or mainly" on the individual (s.127(9)(b)); not one who claimed s.154 (s.127(8)); the certificate with the return (s.127(6)–(7)) and (2)'s scheme conditions are entry conditions. ChapterEightNode allows the lesser of the amount spent or deposited and this limit — "up to" read as a ceiling (OQ-19); more than one disabled dependant is refused (OQ-19). rulebook DED-80DD-001. Old regime only (s.202(2)(a)(xii), p.227). TY 2026-27 and TY 2025-26; the 1961 counterpart, s.80DD, is the TY 2025-26 version (W-075d3). D-138. The "lesser of" is in the cap since W-075d3 (LeastOf), not the node (D-146). TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.80DD(1) (thc p.343): a resident individual who has incurred expenditure for the medical treatment, training and rehabilitation of a dependant with disability, or paid or deposited under an approved scheme, "be allowed a deduction of a sum of seventy-five thousand rupees" — a FIXED sum (Fixed 75000), unlike TY 2026-27's "up to" (the LeastOf above; OQ-19); nothing spent or deposited gives nothing (the node). FA 2022 s.21 (p.28) changes only the scheme's payout (2)(a), (3A). sources/2026-10-07-chapter-via.md B14, M9. D-146.

introducedBy.instrumentCitation: Finance Act, 2022 (6 of 2022), s.21 — s.80DD(2)(a), (3A) (the scheme's payout); s.80DD(1) as subs. by Act 20 of 2015, s.20 (w.e.f. 1-4-2016)
